chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who prays and inserts his hands beneath his garment.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is another garment upon him, either a loin cloth or trousers, then there is no problem; and if there is not, then it is not permissible for him; and if he inserts one hand and does not insert the other, then there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to put hands under the shirt during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions for covering the 'awrah during prayer, emphasizing that the permissibility of tucking hands under the thawb depends on the presence of an undergarment to maintain modesty. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of ensuring complete coverage of the body parts required for valid prayer, balancing ease with decorum. The distinction highlights the importance of intentionality and physical preparation in the ritual act of worship.
